open.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
There you are. Dot said you'd be the new ones. You've got the look. Gus's teams always had it, like you'd been out in weather.
pearl
I'm Pearl. I'm across the street and I'm in and out, and nobody's asked me to leave in thirty years, so don't start.
teddy
She brought a pie. There's a pie on the counter.

passives.line: She looks at the wagon through the window every time she passes it. Not at you. At the wagon.
Dodrill. There's a Dodrill on the Flatwoods witness list, in Gus's hand, 1952. She'd have been a girl.

options.text: You've seen a lot of teams go out that door.

fail.line: Enough to know not to say which ones I liked. Eat your pie.

options.text: Does Dot let you in, or do you let yourself?

pie.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
Apple. It's February, so it's last year's apples, and you'll not know the difference.
pearl
Gus liked apple. I made one every time she drove out and one every time she came back. I've one in the freezer still.

teams.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
Nine. Dot counts seven that came back the same. I count different. I count the ones that came back and didn't go out again.
pearl
You'll go out. The question's the second time.
miriam
That's a better metric than Dot's. Don't tell Dot I said so.

dot.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
Dot lets me in. Dot lets me think I let myself in. That's thirty years of Dot.
pearl
She's softer than the counter. Don't tell her I said. She'll say I'm wrong, and she'll be right.
ruth
Two women have run this town between them and neither one would admit it.

hub.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
Well. I've all afternoon, and so has the pie.

static.line: The pie's her reason to be in the building. Ask her the real one.

options.text: Dodrill. You were on the hill at Flatwoods.
You look at the wagon every time, Pearl. Why?
One in the freezer. For her.

flatwoods.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
I was twelve. My brother dragged me up. Everybody says the smell and the lights, and I'll say it too.
pearl
What I remember is after. A man in a hat told my mother I'd been scared by an owl, and she thanked him, and I stopped talking for a year.
pearl
Gus was the one who asked me what I'd seen. First and only. I've been across the street from her ever since.
elijah
That's the rule. Before the rule had a card.

flatwoods_fail.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
There's Dodrills all over Braxton County. I was a child. Eat.
pearl
Ask the Rainey kid about Flatwoods, if you want it from somebody who'll talk. Everybody else here paints it out.

wagon.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
...Because it's hers. Same wagon. They brought it back from Gallipolis on a flatbed, and Walter said sell it, and Dot said no.
pearl
Every time it goes out I think, this is the one that brings her back. It's a silly thing for an old woman to think.
pearl
Bring it back with the tank full. That's all I ask.
teddy
That's all she asks. Pearl, that's not a small ask.

wagon_fail.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
I look at a car. People look at cars.
pearl
You've a case to drive to. Dot's got the letter. Go on, before the pie goes cold on you.

freezer.speaker: pearl
lines: pearl
For her. I know she's not coming. I knew in '68.
pearl
You keep a pie for someone, it's not for them. It's so you've something to do with your hands the day you hear.
teddy
Pearl, I'm going to need to write that down.
pearl
Write it down, then. Somebody should.
